text.p: Brisbane-based Morgan Stockbroking Ltd was recommending Evans Deakin Industries Ltd as a buy reflecting future strong earnings growth following the successful bid for Clyde Industries Ltd.
"Evans Deakin now has core strengths in a wide number of market sectors. We expect strong earnings growth to emerge after 1996/97," analyst John Clifford said in a research report.
"The combined (EDI-Clyde) group will be a major force in engineering in Australia with annual sales in excess of A$750 million," Clifford said.
After consolidation, the combined group's balance sheet would be carrying debt of about A$98 milion giving a gearing ratio of 52 percent, he said.
"This should be reduced significantly once the sale of Clyde Chemicals is finalised which is expected to fetch $40 million," Clifford said.
While medium-term prospects for the enlarged group were bright, benefits from the acquisition would not translate into earnings until 1997/98, Clifford said.
Clifford was forecasting net profits rising to A$24.7 million in the year ended June 30, 1998 from an estimated A$20 million in the year to June, 1997.
"We have also forecast earnings per share of 22.4 cents in 1996/97, rising to 27.7 cents the following year," he said.
Clifford said the year ended June 1998 would be the first full year of operation for the combined group with most of the non-core asset sales and corresponding debt reduction finalised by then.
"We also expect the Clyde railway division to return to reasonable levels of profitability in that year, given the large number of potential contracts which have been identified," Clifford said.
